definition: AMiner (formerly ArnetMiner) is a free online service used to index, search, and mine big scientific data..
details: AMiner (formerly ArnetMiner) is a free online service used to index, search, and mine big scientific data.

explainer.lead: AMiner is a free online service for searching academic publications and exploring connections among researchers, conferences, and papers. It turns information gathered from the web and digital libraries into a searchable research network, supporting tasks such as finding experts, recommending reviewers, and analysing trends.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a giant library that also draws a map showing which writers, papers, and meetings are connected. AMiner builds that map by collecting researcher profiles and publications, then helps people find experts or see research trends. It was formerly called ArnetMiner.
tiers.practitioner: AMiner can be used for expert finding, association and geographic search, trend analysis, reviewer recommendation, and topic modelling. Its pipeline automatically extracts web profiles and digital-library publications, integrates them in a researcher network knowledge base, and applies social network analysis. Name matches need care because researcher names are the identifiers and ambiguity is handled probabilistically; publication extraction also relies on heuristic rules.
tiers.paperLevel: AMiner constructs a researcher network knowledge base (RNKB) by extracting researcher profiles from web pages and publications from online digital libraries, then integrating the records using researcher names as identifiers. A probabilistic framework addresses name ambiguity, while social network analysis over researchers, conferences, and publications supports expert finding, association search, trend analysis, and topic modelling. The pipeline depends on automatically collected profiles and heuristic publication extraction.

explainer.example: A conference organizer could use AMiner's paper-reviewer recommendation to find candidate reviewers, then use association search to explore connections among relevant researchers, conferences, and publications.

usedIn.name: Academic research
usedIn.detail: Used to identify relationships among researchers and draw statistical correlations about research.

usedIn.detail: AMiner has been used within Elsevier's SciVerse platform.

usedIn.name: Academic conferences
usedIn.detail: The service has been used at conferences including SIGKDD, ICDM, PKDD, and WSDM.

explainer.intuition: A publication list shows individual works, but a research network shows how people, papers, and conferences relate. AMiner builds that network automatically so searches can answer questions about expertise, associations, and trends as well as locate publications.
howItWorks: Collect relevant researcher pages from the web and publications from online digital libraries.
Extract profile data with a unified approach and publication data with heuristic rules.
Integrate profiles and publications using researcher names, with a probabilistic framework for name ambiguity.
Store the integrated records in a researcher network knowledge base.
Use social network analysis to support searches, recommendations, evaluations, and topic modelling.
explainer.whyItMatters: AMiner makes large collections of scientific information useful beyond keyword search by exposing relationships across the research landscape. This supports practical academic tasks such as finding experts, recommending reviewers, evaluating performance, and following trends.
misconceptions: It is not only a publication search engine; it also mines connections among researchers, conferences, and publications.
Identical researcher names are not automatically treated as unambiguous identities; AMiner uses a probabilistic approach to the problem.
AMiner and ArnetMiner are not separate services: AMiner is the later name.
